correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the product operator on tensor inputs from the two one-parameter principal values. For each factor, homogeneity plus a first-order far-field expansion yields a rescaled superlevel-set limit; polar coordinates give the exact coefficient. A proved product-tail lemma then gives the unique logarithmic leading term. Standard L^p boundedness controls high-amplitude pieces. All quantifiers, boundary regimes, and the zero-mass exclusion are explicit; no finite experiment is used for an infinite or asymptotic claim.

value.rationale: The new 2026 p>1 theorem naturally raises the endpoint question, and the modern global endpoint theory identifies L log L as the correct scale. The accepted result supplies a structural mechanism and exact constant for an infinite, canonical smooth subclass, showing that the logarithm is not an artifact of rough angular data.
